html:
Ľudovít Štúr was the leader of the Slovak national revival, born in 1815 in Uhrovec and dead in 1856. In 1843 he and his friends chose the central Slovak dialect as the basis of a written Slovak language.

Before him educated Slovaks wrote in Latin, Hungarian, German or Czech. Štúr's standard, slightly reformed later, is the Slovak written today. He edited the first Slovak political newspaper and sat in the Hungarian diet. In the revolution of 1848 he led a Slovak volunteer revolt against the Hungarian government, hoping for self-rule under the Austrian crown. Its failure left him isolated, and he died after a hunting accident. His circle of poets shaped Slovak national culture.
